# Migration - [`--patch-module`](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/specs/man/java.html#extra-options-for-java)

There can be a situation when two modules that share the same package are needed
by the application. The Java Modules System does not allow two modules to have
the same package. In such cases the `--patch-module` can be used to merge two
JAR files (or modules) into one. Consider the following three JAR files as shown
in the following table.

| Packages      | `domain.jar` | `common.jar` | `app.jar` | Split Package |
| ------------- | :----------: | :----------: | :-------: | :-----------: |
| `demo.app`    |      NO      |      NO      |  **YES**  |      NO       |
| `demo.domain` |   **YES**    |      NO      |    NO     |      NO       |
| `demo.common` |   **YES**    |   **YES**    |    NO     |    **YES**    |

The `app.jar` depends on both the `domain.jar` and `common.jar`, which share the
package `demo.common` (for demonstration purposes). We can use the
`--patch-module` command line option to merge both modules into one.

> ```
> --patch-module module=file(;file)*
> ```
>
> Overrides or augments a module with classes and resources in JAR files or
> directories.
([reference](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/specs/man/java.html#extra-options-for-java))

This should be considered as a **temporary solution** until the modules are
properly updated and the packages are not shared anymore. This can be tricky
when it comes to third-party dependencies which are publicly used and outside of
our control.

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

## Run the example

1. Build the application

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean package
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the JAR file was created and copied to the
   `./target/libs` directory.

   ```shell
   tree --sort=name './target/libs'
   ```

   The application JAR files

   ```
   ./target/libs
   ├── app.jar
   ├── common.jar
   └── domain.jar

   1 directory, 3 files
   ```

2. List all modules

   ```shell
   java --module-path './target/libs' --list-modules
   ```

   All modules available on the module path

3. Describe the JAR files

   Describe the `common.jar`

   ```shell
   jar --describe-module --file './target/libs/common.jar'
   ```

   The common module description

   ```
   demo.common@1.0.0 jar:file:///./target/libs/common.jar!/module-info.class
   exports demo.common
   requires java.base mandated
   ```

   Describe the `domain.jar`

   ```shell
   jar --describe-module --file './target/libs/domain.jar'
   ```

   The domain module description

   ```
   demo.domain@1.0.0 jar:file:///./target/libs/domain.jar!/module-info.class
   exports demo.common
   exports demo.domain
   requires java.base mandated
   ```

   Describe the `app.jar`

   ```shell
   jar --describe-module --file './target/libs/app.jar'
   ```

   The application module description

   ```
   No module descriptor found. Derived automatic module.

   demo.app automatic
   requires java.base mandated
   contains demo.app
   main-class demo.app.Main
   ```

4. Run the application

   ```shell
   java \
     --module-path './target/libs' \
     --module demo.app
   ```

   The application fails to launch because the `demo.domain` (`domain.jar`) and
   `demo.common` (`common.jar`) modules share the same package name.

   ```
   Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: demo/common/StringUtils
       at demo.app/demo.app.Main.main(Main.java:10)
   Caused by: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: demo.common.StringUtils
       at java.base/jdk.internal.loader.BuiltinClassLoader.loadClass(BuiltinClassLoader.java:580)
       at java.base/java.lang.ClassLoader.loadClass(ClassLoader.java:490)
       ... 1 more
   ```

   Patch the `demo.domain` module to include the contents of the `common.jar`
   module using the `--patch-module` command line option.

   ```shell
   java \
     --module-path './target/libs' \
     --add-modules demo.domain \
     --patch-module 'demo.domain=./target/libs/common.jar' \
     --module demo.app
   ```

   This will work, but produces a warning as the `module-info.class` exists in
   both JAR files.

   ```
   "Learn from yesterday, live for today, hope for tomorrow. The important thing is not to stop questioning."
   by ALBERT EINSTEIN
   WARNING: module-info.class ignored in patch: ./target/libs/common.jar
   ```

   Note that the `demo.domain` module export list is a superset of the
   `demo.common` export list. Try the other way round. Patch the `demo.common`
   module to include the contents of the `domain.jar` module using the
   `--patch-module` command line option.

   ```shell
   java \
     --module-path './target/libs' \
     --add-modules demo.common \
     --patch-module 'demo.common=./target/libs/domain.jar' \
     --module demo.app
   ```

   This time the application will not work.

   ```
   WARNING: module-info.class ignored in patch: ./target/libs/domain.jar
   Exception in thread "main" java.lang.IllegalAccessError: class demo.app.Main (in module demo.app) cannot access class demo.domain.Quote (in module demo.common) because module demo.common does not export demo.domain to module demo.app
       at demo.app/demo.app.Main.main(Main.java:11)
   ```

   The application was not able to find the `demo.domain.Quote` as the
   `demo.domain` package is not exported by the `demo.common` module. Export the
   `demo.domain` package using the `--add-exports` command line option.

   ```shell
   java \
     --module-path './target/libs' \
     --add-modules demo.common \
     --patch-module 'demo.common=./target/libs/domain.jar' \
     --add-exports demo.common/demo.domain=demo.app \
     --module demo.app
   ```

   The application works the same and prints the following.

   ```
   "Learn from yesterday, live for today, hope for tomorrow. The important thing is not to stop questioning."
   by ALBERT EINSTEIN
   WARNING: module-info.class ignored in patch: ./target/libs/domain.jar
   ```

   The warning remains as the `module-info.class` file exists in both JAR files.
